title: The Four Words People Read as a Curse — and the Half of Them Everyone Drops
excerpt: The phrase qatalahumu-llah — quoted as proof the Quran curses its enemies — appears in exactly two verses (9:30, 63:4), both ending the same way. The commentators do read it as an imprecation, but its verb is the figurative Form III "fight-against," and the half everyone drops — anna yu'fakun, "how are they so deluded" — recurs three more times with no curse at all.
seo_title: What Does "Qatalahumu-llah" Mean? Quran 9:30 and 63:4 in Full
seo_description: "May God curse them" (qatalahumu-llah) appears in exactly two Quran verses, 9:30 and 63:4. A corpus-verified reading: the classical imprecation, the Form III verb, and the astonishment half — anna yu'fakun — that recurs curse-free at 5:75, 29:61, 43:87.
